name: חילוק שברים רציונליים – פירוק מכנה ריבועי וצמצום (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

questiontext:
Express the following as a single fraction:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}\div\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}. \]

(Hint: Try factorising the fractions.)

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Factorise the quadratic denominator, turn the division into multiplication by the reciprocal, and cancel the common bracket.
Step 1 — Factorise
When dividing fractions you can save work if the denominator or numerator of one fraction has common factors with the denominator or numerator respectively. Factorising these fractions (two numbers with product \({{CT:4}}\) and sum \({{CT:5}}\)) gives:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:6}}\div\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}. \]

Step 2 — Cancel
It is clear that the factor \({{CT:7}}\) is common in both fractions and so we can cancel \({{CT:7}}\) (dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal \(\frac{{CT:3}}{{CT:2}}\), so the bracket appears on the top and on the bottom):

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:8}}\div{{CT:2}} = {{CT:9}}. \]

[[if test="{{CT:12}}"]]The numbers \({{CT:10}}\) and \({{CT:2}}\) have the common factor \({{CT:11}}\), which cancels as well.[[/if]]

on_false.feedback: Your answer is a single fraction but it is not expressed in its simplest terms.
